title: Russell Beats Verstappen for Azerbaijan GP Win as Colapinto Crashes Gasly and Norris【Autosport】
body:
Mercedes driver George Russell clinched a pole‑to‑flag triumph at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku, securing his third victory of the 2026 Formula 1 season. The Briton held off a late‑stage charge from Red Bull’s Max Verstappen despite two safety‑car periods that shuffled the field, while rookie Oliver Colapinto’s aggressive move on Pierre Gasly resulted in a dramatic collision that also involved Lando Norris. Russell’s win narrows the championship gap and re‑energises the title fight as the calendar moves toward the summer stretch.

From the start, Russell demonstrated why he secured pole position, posting a blistering lap of 1:41.395 that left the rest of the grid trailing. His Mercedes displayed a perfect blend of straight‑line speed on the long Baku straight and stability through the twisty, high‑speed sections that characterize the street circuit. As the lights went out, Russell launched ahead, building a comfortable lead while Verstappen, starting from third, struggled to find rhythm in the early laps, losing time behind the midfield pack.

The race’s first safety car emerged on lap 14 after a multi‑car incident at Turn 12, triggered by a sudden tyre failure on a midfield contender. The neutralisation gave Verstappen an opportunity to close the gap, but the Red Bull driver elected to stay on the lead lap rather than pit, preserving track position but sacrificing fresh rubber. When the field restarted, Russell’s pace remained unassailable, extending his lead to over three seconds within a handful of laps.

A second safety car, this time caused by a spectacular collision involving Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Williams rookie Oliver Colapinto, added further intrigue. Colapinto, attempting an overtake on the inside of Turn 8, misjudged the braking zone and clipped Gasly’s rear, sending the Frenchman into the barriers. The ensuing impact also collected Lando Norris, who was forced to retire after sustaining suspension damage. The incident prompted a brief red‑flag period, during which teams scrambled to adjust strategies. Mercedes elected to keep Russell out on his original set of medium tyres, trusting the driver’s ability to manage tyre wear, while Red Bull finally brought Verstappen in for a fresh set of ultrasofts.

The final stint saw Verstappen charge hard, clocking lap times a half‑second quicker than Russell’s, but the Mercedes driver’s disciplined tyre management and clean lines through Baku’s demanding corners allowed him to maintain a slender lead. As the checkered flag approached, Verstappen closed to within 0.8 seconds, prompting a tense final lap where both drivers pushed the limits of their machinery. Russell held his composure, crossing the finish line first, with Verstappen a close second and Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc completing the podium in third.

Russell’s victory carries significant implications for the championship narrative. Prior to Baku, he trailed the reigning champion by 12 points; the win narrows the deficit to just five, intensifying the battle for the title as the series heads into the high‑speed circuits of Austria and the historic streets of Monaco. Verstappen, while disappointed, demonstrated that Red Bull remains a threat, especially when tyre strategy aligns with his aggressive driving style. Meanwhile, the incident involving Colapinto, Gasly and Norris highlights the fine line between bold overtaking and costly errors on narrow street tracks, a factor teams will weigh heavily in future races.

Looking ahead, the next few rounds will test the adaptability of the leading teams. Mercedes must continue to extract performance from a car that has shown strong qualifying pace but occasional vulnerability under changing conditions. Red Bull, meanwhile, will seek to capitalise on their superior straight‑line speed and Verstappen’s racecraft to reclaim lost ground. For the midfield, the Baku drama serves as a reminder that opportunities—and setbacks—can arrive in an instant, shaping the midfield tussle for valuable points. As the season progresses, the championship is poised to remain an open contest, with Russell’s Baku triumph adding fresh momentum to a tightly contested title chase.
